code_quality.title: Split massive ai-query-service.ts into focused modules
code_quality.description: The file src/domains/ai-query/ai-query-service.ts has grown to 2,129 lines and handles at least 8 distinct responsibilities: Ollama API communication, intent detection, question parsing, tracker creation, log entry creation, data retrieval, period detection, and fuzzy matching. This severely violates the Single Responsibility Principle.
code_quality.rationale: Files over 500 lines become hard to navigate, test, and maintain. At 2,129 lines, this file requires developers to hold too much context in their heads. Breaking it into focused modules will improve testability, make code reviews easier, and reduce the risk of introducing bugs when making changes.
code_quality.currentState: Single 2,129-line file containing: queryOllama(), detectPeriods(), parseQuestion(), detectIntent(), handleEntryCreation(), createLogEntry(), answerQuestion(), getRelevantData(), createTracker(), fuzzy matching logic, and more
code_quality.proposedChange:
Split into focused modules:
- src/domains/ai-query/ollama-client.ts (API communication, ~100 lines)
- src/domains/ai-query/intent-detector.ts (intent detection & parsing, ~300 lines)
- src/domains/ai-query/tracker-creator.ts (tracker creation logic, ~200 lines)
- src/domains/ai-query/log-entry-service.ts (log entry creation, ~150 lines)
- src/domains/ai-query/question-parser.ts (question parsing & fuzzy matching, ~400 lines)
- src/domains/ai-query/data-retriever.ts (data gathering, ~300 lines)
- src/domains/ai-query/period-detector.ts (period detection, ~100 lines)
- src/domains/ai-query/types.ts (shared interfaces)
code_quality.bestPractice: Single Responsibility Principle - each module should have one reason to change. Files should generally be under 300-500 lines for maintainability.
prerequisites: Ensure comprehensive test coverage before refactoring
Review all imports/exports to maintain API compatibility

code_quality.title: Remove duplicate StatsProcessor implementations
code_quality.description: The files src/domains/stats/statsV5.ts (555 lines) and src/domains/stats/stats-processor.class.ts (551 lines) contain nearly identical implementations of the StatsProcessor class. Both files have the same imports, same class structure, same constructor, same init() method, and same properties. This is a significant code duplication issue.
code_quality.rationale: Duplicate code leads to bugs being fixed in one place but not the other, doubles maintenance effort, and creates confusion about which implementation to use. This duplication likely arose from a refactoring attempt that was never completed.
code_quality.currentState: Two nearly identical files (~1,100 lines total) both implementing StatsProcessor class with same properties: trackable, rows, type, math, avg, sum, chart, dow, tod, min, max, fromDate, toDate, mode, is24Hour, streak, valueMap
code_quality.proposedChange:
1. Identify any differences between the two implementations
2. Consolidate into a single stats-processor.class.ts file
3. Update all imports to use the consolidated version
4. Remove the duplicate file
5. Consider if both files exist due to a failed migration (statsV5 suggests versioning)
code_quality.bestPractice: DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself) - eliminate code duplication to reduce maintenance burden and prevent inconsistent behavior
prerequisites: Run tests to verify which implementation is actually used
Check git history to understand why duplication exists

code_quality.title: Reduce excessive 'any' type usage for better type safety
code_quality.description: Found 94 occurrences of ': any' across 30+ files in the codebase. While TypeScript is configured with some strict options (noUnusedLocals, noImplicitReturns, allowUnreachableCode: false), the extensive use of 'any' undermines type safety. High-impact files include: trackable-element.ts (9), interact.ts (9), dymoji.ts (9), import.n2.ts (7), remote.ts (5).
code_quality.rationale: Excessive 'any' usage defeats the purpose of TypeScript, allowing runtime errors that could be caught at compile time. Each 'any' is a potential bug hiding spot where the compiler can't help catch mistakes. Proper typing improves IDE autocomplete, refactoring safety, and code documentation.
code_quality.currentState: 94 occurrences of ': any' across the codebase, disabling type checking for return values, parameters, and variables
code_quality.proposedChange:
1. Enable stricter TypeScript options: "strict": true or "noImplicitAny": true in tsconfig.json
2. Prioritize fixing 'any' in core modules: trackable-element.ts, interact.ts, stores
3. Replace 'any' with proper interfaces or union types
4. Use 'unknown' instead of 'any' when type is truly unknown, then use type guards
5. Create proper type definitions for external APIs and dynamic data
code_quality.bestPractice: Use TypeScript's type system to catch errors at compile time. Prefer 'unknown' over 'any' for truly unknown types, and use type guards to narrow types safely.
prerequisites: Start with a single high-impact module to establish patterns
Add type definitions incrementally to avoid overwhelming PR sizes

code_quality.title: Consolidate fragmented stats implementations (stats vs stats2)
code_quality.description: The codebase has two separate stats directories: src/domains/stats/ (12 files, ~1,400 lines) and src/domains/stats2/ (6 files, ~500 lines). Both implement statistical calculations with overlapping functionality including Stats2Store.ts, day-of-week calculations, and time formatting. The 'stats2' naming suggests an incomplete migration or parallel development.
code_quality.rationale: Having two stats implementations creates confusion about which to use, leads to inconsistent behavior, and doubles maintenance effort. The naming convention (stats vs stats2) suggests technical debt from an unfinished refactoring effort. New developers won't know which implementation is canonical.
code_quality.currentState:
Two separate stats implementations with unclear boundaries:
- stats/: StatsProcessor class, StatsStore, stats-functions, time-of-day
- stats2/: Stats2Store (197 lines), day-of-week, time-formats
Note: stats/statsV5.ts imports from stats2/day-of-week, showing tight coupling
code_quality.proposedChange:
1. Audit both implementations to understand feature differences
2. Identify which features are used where in the application
3. Create a unified stats module with clear separation of concerns:
   - src/domains/stats/processor/ - core calculation logic
   - src/domains/stats/store/ - state management
   - src/domains/stats/time/ - time-related utilities (day-of-week, time-of-day)
4. Deprecate and remove the redundant implementation
5. Update all imports across the codebase
code_quality.codeExample:
// Current (fragmented):
import StatsProcessor from '../stats/statsV5'
import getDayOfWeek from '../stats2/day-of-week'
import { Stats2Store } from '../stats2/Stats2Store'
import { StatsStore } from '../stats/StatsStore'

// Proposed (unified):
import { StatsProcessor } from '../stats/processor'
import { StatsStore } from '../stats/store'
import { getDayOfWeek, getTimeOfDay } from '../stats/time-utils'
code_quality.bestPractice: Single Source of Truth - each concept should have exactly one authoritative implementation. Version suffixes (V5, 2) in production code suggest incomplete migrations.
prerequisites: Complete the duplicate StatsProcessor fix first (cq-002)
Create comprehensive tests for both implementations before merging
